name: CNSA 2.0
reference: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite Profile for SSH (draft-becker-cnsa2-ssh-profile-02): 'Any algorithm other than ML-KEM-1024 MUST NOT be negotiated for key exchange in a CNSA-compliant connection.'
summary: The quantum-resistant suite for US national security systems: ML-KEM-1024 key exchange, ML-DSA-87 signatures and AES-256-GCM, with no classical fallback permitted.
notes: Expect this to fail on every server today: the SSH profile is still an IETF Internet-Draft and mainstream implementations do not yet offer mlkem1024-sha384 or ssh-mldsa87. A failure here measures the migration gap, not a misconfiguration. NSA's timeline requires new national security system acquisitions to support CNSA 2.0 from January 2027 and to use it exclusively by the early 2030s; cnsa-1.0 is the transitional profile that current software can actually meet.

kex.reason: The profile permits ML-KEM-1024 alone; no other method, including a hybrid, may be negotiated.

cipher.reason: AES-256-GCM only, with the full 16-octet authentication tag. The draft names AEAD_AES_256_GCM (RFC 5647) and aes256-gcm@openssh.com as the two acceptable encryption identifiers.

mac.reason: Integrity comes from the AES-256-GCM tag; no separate MAC is negotiated.
